survivors.claim: The s0 fix makes every mock-scope refresh() rebuild whichever card is open, so a refresh triggered by something other than that card's own Reply — the deferred Approve/Reject/Delete toast POST from a previously closed card, the strip row's Resolve button, or the box-layer `a` key — wipes an in-progress reply draft in the open card and drops its focus. Executed: Approve on N1's card (toast pending), open N2's card, type `draft on N2` (textarea focused); when N1's deferred POST fired 5s later, N2's card was rebuilt with `ta: ""` and `active: null`. This is a regression introduced by the fix (before it, refresh() never touched cardSlot). Not spec-contradicting text (no Decision promises a draft survives another note's toast) and no runtime error, so advisory; a fix would skip the rebuild when the open card's textarea is non-empty or scope the rebuild to the note the POST just touched.
survivors.impact: An owner who approves one note and, within the five-second undo window, opens another note and starts typing a reply loses what they typed the moment the first approval lands, with no warning.
survivors.evidence: Headless Chromium against a served fixture (N1 open+thread, N2 open, N3 open): r1_N2_beforeToastFires {msgs:["N2 text"], ta:"draft on N2", active:"TEXTAREA", toast:"ApprovedUndo"} -> after sleep(5600): r1_N2_afterToastFires {msgs:["N2 text"], ta:"", active:null, toast:null}. Hunk: `if (selectedNoteId != null) { var openNote = mockNotes.filter(...)[0]; if (openNote) openNoteCard(openNote) }` runs on every mock-scope refresh().
